newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - underperforming Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - underperforming Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained about 1/4 to 3/8 at midday Wednesday, but stopped well short of the much steeper gains in Treasuries.

"It seems like there's activity, but not a lot of going-away," one muni trader said. "A lot of the institutional buyers are on the sidelines," he added, but said there was some interest in new issue deals.
Treasury prices are at session highs at midday, adding to gains scored after market-friendly data on inflation.
The Labor Department said consumer prices in June rose just 0.1 percent overall, versus expectations for a 0.2 percent rise.
The figure was another piece of reassuring news for investors counting on inflation to remain tame, and again offered validation for the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady.
The government long bond was up 25/32 at 101-26/32, pushing the yield down to 6.49 percent.

In new issue news, Merrill Lynch & Co. said it postponed until Thursday a Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corp refunding deal expected today. The firm also raised the amount to $162 million from $120 million.
Bear Stearns & Co. said it repriced $38 million Methodist Health Systems, Tenn., bonds, cutting yields and lowering the par amount from $47 million.
Earlier deals included the United Nations Development Corp's $162 million issue, which Goldman Sachs & Co said it tentatively priced at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2026.

On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $144 million were scheduled. Raymond James & Associates won the largest, a $41 million Texas Public Facilities Authority deal, and reoffered the 2015 maturity at 5.25 percent. The 2017 was not formally reoffered.
The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue list, a gauge of the secondary market, rose to $1.056 billion from $955 million on Tuesday.
September municipal bond futures rose 22/32 to 120-6/32, while September Treasury bond futures gained 21/32 to 114-19/32. The MOB spread widened to 179 ticks from 178 at the close on Tuesday.
In the secondary market, bids on Bexar County, Texas, MBIA 5-1/4s of 2027 were down one basis point to 5.52 percent.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2027 were down two basis points to 5.37 percent.
